steps.title: Gate core: PBO, PSR, DSR, MinTRL with proofs
steps.goal: Implement the statistics and prove them against known answers.
steps.prompt:
Implement in quantgate/stats.py: pbo_cscv(R: ndarray[T, N], S: int = 16, metric=sharpe) returning pbo, logits, and performance degradation slope; psr(sr, n, skew, kurt, sr_benchmark=0); dsr(sr, n, skew, kurt, n_trials, var_trial_sr); min_trl(sr, skew, kurt, sr_benchmark, prob=0.95). Use non-annualized per-period Sharpe internally; annualize only in reports.

Proofs, written to proof.md with numbers: (a) reproduce the DSR paper's worked example to 3 decimals; (b) N=100 pure-noise strategies, T=2000, seeds 0-19: report the PBO distribution and confirm no strategy passes DSR at 0.95; (c) planted signal: one strategy with true per-period Sharpe 0.1 among 99 noise strategies: PBO near 0 and DSR passes; (d) run pypbo on the same matrices and report agreement to 2 decimals or explain differences; (e) hypothesis property tests: PBO in [0, 1], PSR monotone in sr, DSR decreasing in n_trials.

steps.title: Purged and combinatorial cross-validation
steps.goal: Provide leakage-free splits and prove they remove leakage.
steps.prompt:
Implement quantgate/cv.py: PurgedKFold(n_splits, embargo_frac) taking a pandas Series of label end times (t1) indexed by start time, yielding train and test indices with training samples whose label interval overlaps the test interval removed and an embargo after each test block; CombinatorialPurgedCV(n_groups, k_test) yielding all C(n_groups, k_test) splits and a method to assemble backtest paths. Follow the book's definitions recorded in sources.md.

Leakage proof: generate a synthetic series with triple-barrier-style labels spanning 20 bars and features that are noise but share label windows with neighbors. Train a RandomForestClassifier with sklearn KFold (shuffled) versus PurgedKFold. Plain KFold should show accuracy clearly above 0.5; purged should be near 0.5. Report both with 10 seeds. Add unit tests: no train index overlaps any test label window; embargo honored; number of CPCV paths equals the formula.
steps.expect: quantgate/cv.py, tests passing, a leakage table in proof.md (plain versus purged accuracy, 10 seeds).
steps.audit: If purged accuracy is still well above 0.5 on noise, leakage remains; inspect t1 handling. Confirm the embargo length used later will be at least the maximum pairs holding period.

steps.title: OU pairs with Kalman hedge ratio
steps.goal: Build the strategy from the list with honest costs.
steps.prompt:
Pull hourly candles and funding history from the Hyperliquid info API for BTC, ETH, SOL, HYPE perps, maximum available history; cache parquet. Split time: first 60% training, last 40% held out.

On training data only, screen pairs ETH/BTC, SOL/ETH, HYPE/SOL, and all other combinations with Engle-Granger and Johansen tests on log prices; record every pair tested (they count as trials). For survivors: static OLS beta, OU MLE fit on the residual spread (theta, mu, sigma, half-life ln(2)/theta). Kalman version: state beta_t (and intercept) with random-walk transition; tune process-noise delta on training only.

Rules: enter when spread z-score exceeds k, exit at z=0 or after a max hold of 3 half-lives, stop at z of 2k. Costs: Hyperliquid taker fee per leg per side, funding paid or received hourly per leg. Grid: k in {1.5, 2, 2.5}, delta in 5 values, lookback for z in 3 values. Log every combination's per-period returns as one column of the trial matrix.
steps.expect: pairs/ code, data cache, screen.md with all pairs tested and test statistics, a trial return matrix for the gate, held-out cointegration retest results.
steps.audit: Re-test cointegration on held-out data for each survivor; a pair not cointegrated out of sample is reported as failed, not dropped silently. Confirm funding is applied with the correct sign for long and short legs on 5 hand-checked hours.

steps.title: Run the gate, compare controls, paper arm
steps.goal: Judge the strategy with the gate and forward evidence.
steps.prompt:
Using the trial matrix from step 4 on training data, compute PBO via CSCV with S=16. Select the in-sample best configuration. On held-out data compute its Sharpe, PSR, DSR with n_trials equal to every combination and pair evaluated, and MinTRL. Run CombinatorialPurgedCV with embargo at least the max hold to get a distribution of path Sharpes.

Controls on held-out data: static OLS beta with the same rules, and flat (no position, zero return). The strategy must beat static beta to justify the Kalman filter and beat flat after costs.

Gate: PBO below 0.2, DSR probability above 0.95, held-out Sharpe CI excluding zero, beats both controls. If and only if it passes, build paper/: a read-only runner on live hourly candles with frozen parameters, logging hypothetical fills at next-bar open plus fees and funding, alongside the static-beta control, for 30 days with a heartbeat file.
steps.expect: gate_run.md with PBO, DSR, PSR, MinTRL, CPCV path distribution, controls table, verdict; paper/ running only if passed.
steps.audit: Confirm n_trials includes screened-out pairs and every grid point. Check that no parameter was refit on held-out data. If the result passes only with the smallest trial count, it does not pass.

steps.title: Validate against oracles, gap report
steps.goal: Confirm the gate is right, the verdict is earned, and list what is missing.
steps.prompt:
Run the oracles and record pass or fail with evidence: (1) DSR paper example reproduced to 3 decimals; (2) noise sets give high PBO and no DSR pass, planted signal gives near-zero PBO and passes; (3) pypbo agrees on PBO to 2 decimals or differences are explained; (4) purged CV removes the plain-KFold leakage on synthetic data; (5) the pairs verdict follows mechanically from the gate thresholds; (6) if passed, 30 days of paper trading beat the static-beta control after fees and funding. Real money stays off unless all six pass; any later pilot is capped at $500 notional, 1x leverage, 10% drawdown halt.

Apply the gate to one real past result, the Oracle Commander rolodex win-rate finding if its trial matrix is available, and report the PBO. Write gap_report.md: each guide claim (PBO highest-leverage, ETH/BTC a good OU candidate, Kalman as reusable smoother, mlfinlab as the purged CV source) and each result, verified / unverified / false with evidence, ranked by impact. Fix the top three.
steps.expect: oracles.md with six rows and evidence, the retro PBO on a real past result or a note on why unavailable, gap_report.md ranked.
steps.audit: Any oracle lacking a number or file is unverified, and an unverified oracle means no-go. Confirm no return projection appears anywhere in the reports.

gap_audit_prompt:
You are an independent reviewer of a quant validation gate and the pairs strategy it judged. You did not build them. Read sources.md, quantgate/, proof.md, screen.md, gate_run.md, oracles.md, and gap_report.md.

1. Enumerate every claim: formula correctness, DSR reproduction, noise and planted-signal PBO behavior, pypbo agreement, leakage removal, cointegration results, trial count, gate verdict, paper results. Mark each verified, unverified, or false. Re-run the DSR example and one noise-set PBO yourself.
2. List missing pieces: trials not counted, embargo shorter than max hold, funding sign errors, held-out data touched during tuning, small-sample HYPE history, no static-beta control.
3. Rank by impact on the chance an overfit strategy reaches capital: trial undercounting and leakage first, then cost errors, then sample size.
4. Fix the top three now and show before and after numbers.
5. Report what you could not fix and why. If any fix changes the verdict, say so first.
Return a claim table (claim, status, evidence, fix) and the ranked gap list. Never project returns.
self_questions: Does my DSR reproduce the paper's worked example, and which variance-of-trial-Sharpes estimate did I use?
Did I count every pair screened and every grid point as a trial?
Is my PBO logit sign convention right, so that noise looks overfit?
Is the embargo at least the longest holding period in the pairs rules?
Are my pairs cointegrated on held-out data, or only in the fitting window?
Does the Kalman hedge beat static OLS beta after fees, or only trade more?
Is funding applied per leg with the right sign, and is it driving the result?
Does HYPE have enough history for MinTRL at the observed Sharpe?
Did pypbo and my implementation agree, and if not, which one is wrong?
Could I apply the gate to the Oracle Commander rolodex result to check it would have caught it?
Is mlfinlab licensed for my use, or did I build purged CV from the book?
validation_oracles: Bailey and Lopez de Prado (2014) DSR worked example reproduced to 3 decimals by quantgate.dsr.
Synthetic proofs: 20 seeds of 100 pure-noise strategies give high PBO with no DSR pass; a planted true-signal strategy gives PBO near 0 and passes DSR.
Independent implementation esvhd/pypbo agrees with quantgate PBO to 2 decimals on the same return matrices.
Leakage test: plain shuffled KFold accuracy clearly above 0.5 on noise features with overlapping labels, purged K-fold near 0.5, across 10 seeds.
If the gate passes: 30-day read-only paper run on live Hyperliquid candles beats the static-beta control after fees and funding.
failure_modes: Trial undercounting. Tell: DSR passes easily; trial count equals grid size only. Fix: include every pair screened and every discarded variant.
Look-ahead through overlapping labels. Tell: CV accuracy far above held-out accuracy. Fix: purged K-fold with embargo at least max hold.
Spurious cointegration. Tell: Engle-Granger passes in training, fails on held-out. Fix: require out-of-sample retest; report failures.
Kalman overfits through process noise. Tell: best delta sits at a grid edge, many more trades than static beta. Fix: widen grid, compare to static beta, count trials.
Funding misapplied. Tell: PnL driven by funding with the wrong sign on short legs. Fix: hand-check hours and separate funding PnL in reports.
License surprise. Tell: mlfinlab import fails or requires a key. Fix: build purged CV from the book, as specified in sources.md.
Gate tuned to pass. Tell: thresholds changed after seeing results. Fix: freeze thresholds in code before step 5 and record the commit.
agent_direction: Gate first: do not touch strategy code until proof.md passes. Cache papers' formulas in sources.md and Hyperliquid data in parquet under data/quant/; never refetch cached ranges. Spawn one sub-agent to implement and test quantgate.stats against the papers and another to independently run pypbo on the same matrices as the agreement oracle. Freeze gate thresholds in code with a commit before running the strategy grid. Never load or print a private key; paper runs are read-only. Stop and ask Victor before any step that would place an order, if the synthetic proofs fail twice, or if no pair is cointegrated out of sample. Write outputs to docs/quant_gate/: sources.md, proof.md, screen.md, gate_run.md, oracles.md, gap_report.md, with code in quantgate/ and pairs/. Return the verdict line first, then the proofs table, then gaps. Never project returns.

mission: Run a structured evaluation of World Labs' Marble (Fei-Fei Li's Large World Model product, closed-source, browser-based) for one concrete job: game-level and previs blockout. Running this produces a prompt set across text, image, and 3D-layout inputs, exported Gaussian splats and GLB collider meshes, a working import into Blender, three.js, and a game engine with walkable collision, measured persistence and export quality, and a comparison against an open alternative. Done means each guide claim is verified or refuted with files and numbers, and a written verdict on where Marble fits in the pipeline.

deeper_not_bigger.professional_would: Treat Marble as a vendor under evaluation, not a toy: write a brief with acceptance criteria before generating anything, keep a fixed prompt set so runs are comparable, and measure outputs with tools that do not care about the demo reel. Check the license terms for commercial use of outputs and what World Labs retains, because a closed cloud service owns the failure modes. Test the persistence claim (the scene does not change when the camera returns) numerically, inspect the collider mesh's triangle count and watertightness, and walk a character controller through it in an engine. Plan the exit: every useful asset must exist as a standard file outside World Labs.

- Comparators: Hunyuan3D-2 and Tripo for single objects; Genie 3 as a non-exporting contrast.

A capsule character walks a predefined path through the collider in Godot or Unity without falling through or snagging, logged. SSIM of 0.98 or higher between renders of the same pose before and after navigating away, in Marble's viewer capture and in the exported splat. A blind preference test by two people comparing Marble output to the open alternative for the same brief.
deeper_not_bigger.rewritten_prompt:
Evaluate World Labs' Marble for game-level and previs blockout, and give me files and numbers rather than impressions.

1. From World Labs' docs and terms, record: input modes, export formats (Gaussian splats as .ply or .spz, GLB mesh, video), credit pricing, whether an API now exists, and the license for commercial use of outputs.

one_shot:
ROLE: You are a technical artist and pipeline TD evaluating a closed commercial 3D generator for a small studio. You judge it by the files it exports and how they behave in real tools, not by its demo reel.

CONTEXT:
- Product: Marble by World Labs (founders Fei-Fei Li, Justin Johnson, Ben Mildenhall, Christoph Lassner). Launched November 2025 as a browser app with waitlist access; closed weights; credit-based pricing.
- Claims to test from the guide: generates persistent explorable environments from text, images, video, or blocky 3D layouts in about 1-3 minutes; represents appearance as 3D Gaussian splats plus a low-poly collider mesh; the scene stays identical when the camera returns, unlike frame-predicting video models (Sora, Veo, Genie 3); exports Gaussian splats (.ply or proprietary), GLB mesh, and rendered video; export quality is good enough for previs, not final pixel; no public API at launch.
- Comparators: Hunyuan3D-2 and Tripo (single objects), Genie 3 (interactive but no export). Tools: Blender 4.x, three.js with a splat renderer such as Spark (sparkjsdev/spark) or similar, Godot 4 or Unity, Khronos glTF Validator, gltf-transform, trimesh, scikit-image SSIM.
- Use case: game-level blockout and film previs.

HARD CONSTRAINTS:
- Fixed prompt set, versioned in prompts.jsonl; no cherry-picking: every generation is logged and scored, including failures.
- Do not upload private or client images; use your own photos or public-domain references.
- Record credits spent per generation and stop at the budget Victor sets.
- Read the terms of service and output license before using any output in a shared project.
- All pipeline steps scripted and headless where possible so results reproduce.

DELIVERABLES, in order:
1. product_facts.md: inputs, exports, formats, pricing, API status, output license, each with a World Labs URL and date checked.
2. brief.md with acceptance criteria: GLB validates with zero errors; collider walkable; splat playback at 60 fps or better on this GPU at 1080p; generation under 3 minutes; usable after Blender import.
3. runs.csv: per prompt, input mode, generation time, credits, export file sizes, splat count, collider triangle count.
4. Validation outputs: gltf-validator reports, gltf-transform inspect output, trimesh watertight and scale checks.
5. pipeline/: Blender headless import and fixed-pose render script; three.js splat viewer page with an fps counter; Godot project with the collider and a capsule controller walking a scripted path.
6. persistence.md: SSIM between renders of the same pose before and after navigating away, in Marble's viewer capture and in the exported splat.
7. compare.md: the same 3 briefs done with an open alternative, judged blind by two reviewers.

GAP ANALYSIS (built in): keep gaps.md. Record anything you could not test (no waitlist access, an export format missing, no layout editor on your plan) and how it limits the verdict. Fill what you can from documentation and community exports; label those as secondhand.

SELF-QUESTIONS before finishing:
- Does the collider mesh align with the splats, or is it offset or scaled?
- What is the real-world scale of exports, and does a 1.8 m capsule fit through doors?
- Do layout-conditioned runs respect my blocked geometry, measured, not eyeballed?
- Is persistence true in the export, or only in the hosted viewer?
- What is the splat count and file size, and does it play at 60 fps here?
- Who owns outputs and can I ship them commercially?
- What happens to my pipeline if World Labs changes pricing or closes access?
- Where does Marble beat the open alternative, and where does it lose?

STOP CONDITIONS: stop and report if there is no access to Marble (deliver the evaluation harness ready to run plus secondhand findings), if the credit budget is reached, or if the terms forbid the intended use.

RETURN FORMAT: markdown report: Verdict (where Marble fits, one paragraph), Product facts, Runs table, Validation, Pipeline results, Persistence, Comparison, Gaps ranked, file paths.

steps.title: Ground truth: product, formats, terms
steps.goal: Know exactly what Marble offers and permits today.
steps.prompt:
From World Labs' site, Marble docs or help center, blog posts, and terms of service, record in product_facts.md: access model (waitlist, plans), input modes (text, image, multi-image, video, 3D layout editor), generation time claims, edit tools, export formats with extensions (splat .ply, .spz, other; GLB collider or full mesh; video), splat attribute layout, credit pricing per generation and per export, whether a public API or SDK exists now (the guide says none at launch), and the output license for commercial use and what World Labs retains.

Also verify supporting tools: does sparkjsdev/spark exist and render the exported splat format; does nianticlabs/spz document .spz; which Blender add-ons import 3D Gaussian splat .ply. Each row: fact, value, URL, date checked. Mark anything from third-party posts as secondhand.
steps.expect: product_facts.md with 15+ sourced rows and a tool-compatibility table.
steps.audit: Rows without a World Labs or repo URL are unverified. If the license forbids commercial use or requires attribution, flag it at the top. If no access is available, mark generation steps blocked and continue building the harness.

steps.title: Brief and fixed prompt set
steps.goal: Define acceptance criteria and comparable inputs before generating.
steps.prompt:
Write brief.md with acceptance criteria for game blockout and previs: GLB passes Khronos glTF Validator with zero errors; collider walkable by a 0.4 m radius, 1.8 m capsule along a scripted path; splat playback at 60 fps or better at 1080p on this machine's GPU; generation under 3 minutes; scale within 10% of real-world for known objects (a door 2.0-2.1 m); Blender import without manual fixes.

Write prompts.jsonl with 18 entries: 10 text prompts spanning interiors (diner at 3am, tea room), exteriors (cyberpunk alley with wet pavement and fog), and game spaces (three-room dungeon with a corridor); 5 image prompts from your own photos or public-domain images with sources recorded; 3 layout prompts where you block out geometry with known dimensions (a 6 x 4 m room with a 1 m doorway centered on one wall). Each entry: id, mode, input, intended use, measurable expectation.
steps.expect: brief.md with 6+ numeric criteria; prompts.jsonl with 18 entries including dimensions for layout prompts.
steps.audit: Every criterion must be measurable by a tool named in methods. Layout prompts must include dimensions so step 4 can measure adherence. Remove any image you do not have the right to upload.

steps.title: Generate and export
steps.goal: Run every prompt once, log everything, export standard files.
steps.prompt:
Run all 18 prompts in Marble in prompts.jsonl order. For each: start and end timestamps, credits used, any errors, and a screenshot of the hosted viewer at a fixed starting view. Export splats in every offered format, the GLB mesh or collider, and a short rendered flythrough. Save under exports/<id>/ with original filenames preserved.

Record in runs.csv: id, mode, generation seconds, credits, splat file size, splat count (parse the .ply header element vertex count, or the .spz header), GLB size, triangle count (from gltf-transform inspect), and notes. Do not regenerate failures to get a better result; a second attempt is a new row labeled retry. Stop when the credit budget is reached and record which prompts were not run.
steps.expect: exports/ with 18 folders (or fewer with budget notes), runs.csv complete, viewer screenshots.
steps.audit: Check that every runs.csv row has a matching export folder and parsed counts; a missing count means the format was not parsed, so fix the parser. Compute median generation time and compare with the 1-3 minute claim.

steps.title: Validate and integrate into Blender, three.js, and a game engine
steps.goal: Prove the exports work in real pipelines.
steps.prompt:
For each GLB: run the Khronos glTF Validator and save the report; run gltf-transform inspect; load with trimesh to check watertightness, bounds, and units. For layout prompts, measure the room and doorway dimensions on the collider and compare with the blocked-out values.

Blender: write pipeline/blender_import.py that imports the GLB (and splats via a chosen add-on), places a camera at 3 fixed poses, and renders with blender -b -P; log errors.

three.js: build pipeline/viewer.html that loads the splat with Spark or another splat renderer and the GLB, and shows an fps counter; record fps at 1080p for each scene.

Game engine: in Godot 4 (or Unity), import the GLB as a static collider, add a 0.4 m radius, 1.8 m capsule CharacterBody3D, and script it along waypoints through the space; log falls through the floor, stuck frames, and doorway passes. Write integration.md with a table per scene.
steps.expect: validator reports, inspect outputs, dimension checks, Blender renders, fps table, Godot run logs, integration.md.
steps.audit: Fail a scene if the validator reports any error, Blender import errors, fps under 60, or the capsule falls through or gets stuck. Check collider-splat alignment by overlaying the GLB wireframe on a splat render; an offset over 5 cm is a defect to record.

steps.title: Persistence test and open-alternative comparison
steps.goal: Test the central persistence claim and benchmark against an alternative.
steps.prompt:
Persistence: for 5 scenes, capture the hosted viewer at a fixed pose, navigate away for at least 20 seconds through other parts of the scene, return to the exact pose (use any coordinate display or a saved view), and capture again. Repeat for the exported splat in viewer.html with a scripted camera. Compute SSIM with scikit-image on aligned grayscale captures. Also reload the scene in a new session and compare. Write persistence.md.

Comparison: pick 3 briefs. Produce the same scenes with an open alternative: an image-to-3D object generator such as Hunyuan3D-2 for hero props assembled in Blender, or an open scene generator if you can run one. Render matched views. Two reviewers who did not make them choose blindly per brief on usefulness for blockout. Record time spent per approach.
steps.expect: persistence.md with SSIM per scene and condition; compare.md with matched renders, blind choices, and time per approach.
steps.audit: If SSIM is below 0.98 in the hosted viewer, check camera pose alignment before concluding non-persistence. Reviewers must not know which tool made which render; record how blinding was done.

steps.title: Validate against oracles, gap report, verdict
steps.goal: Close with evidence and a clear verdict on fit.
steps.prompt:
Run the oracles and record pass or fail with evidence: (1) Khronos glTF Validator zero errors across exported GLBs; (2) Blender headless import and render succeeds for every scene; (3) Godot capsule walks every scripted path without falls or stuck frames; (4) persistence SSIM 0.98 or higher in hosted viewer and export; (5) splat playback at 60 fps at 1080p; (6) blind reviewers' preferences recorded for 3 briefs.

Write gap_report.md: every guide claim (1-3 minute generation, splats plus collider mesh, persistence versus video models, export formats, previs-grade quality, no public API, waitlist access) and every brief criterion, marked verified / unverified / false with evidence, ranked by impact on adopting Marble in the pipeline. Fix the top three where possible (better import script, scale correction, alignment fix). Then write verdict.md: where Marble fits (environment blockout, previs, VR scouting), where it does not, cost per usable scene from runs.csv, license constraints, and the exit plan if access changes.
steps.expect: oracles.md with six rows, gap_report.md ranked, verdict.md with cost per usable scene and exit plan.
steps.audit: Any oracle without a log, render, or report file is unverified. The verdict must cite numbers from runs.csv and integration.md, not impressions.
